entry.description: three-dimensional elliptic-equation regularity counterexamples. the paper constructs smooth uniformly elliptic coefficient matrices and bounded smooth solutions with common boundary data whose gradient l1 norms diverge, ruling out ellipticity-only interior w1,p estimates for every p at least one and producing a locally non-bv measurable-coefficient limit. the authors say the main results and key strategies emerged through chats with chatgpt 5.6 sol; they reworked, rewrote, checked and simplified all arguments.
entry.anchor_claim: There are smooth 3-by-3 coefficient matrices with I <= A_m <= 2^81 I and uniformly bounded smooth solutions with common Dirichlet data for which ||Du_m||_{L^1(B_1)} tends to infinity; hence no ellipticity-only interior W^{1,p} estimate holds for p >= 1, and a uniformly convergent limit need not be locally BV.
entry.prior_rationale: Nadirashvili, Tkachev and Vlăduţ posed the three-dimensional ellipticity-only W^{1,1} question in their 2014 monograph.
entry.advance_rationale: The constructed sequence resolves that question negatively and rules out all stronger W^{1,p} and BV estimates under ellipticity alone.
entry.scope_rationale: The construction is an infinite sequence and extends by dummy variables to every dimension at least three.
entry.resistance_rationale: The literature supplies related regularity and counterexample programs, but the audited source does not pin two independent pre-solution attacks on the exact three-dimensional W^{1,1} target.
entry.age_rationale: Elapsed duration is computed from the coded framing and solution dates; it is not a capability claim.

entry.description: finite entanglement-breaking index for ppt channels. the paper proves every completely positive and completely copositive map has finite entanglement-breaking index and gives a dimension-uniform index-at-most-three result for a larger family containing the 2-superpositive maps. some section 3 proof-development ideas arose in gpt-5.6 sol discussions; the author independently verified and reformulated those suggestions.
entry.anchor_claim: Every PPT map Phi:M_d to M_d has finite entanglement-breaking index: for some N(Phi), every iterate Phi^n with n >= N(Phi) is entanglement breaking; moreover the paper identifies a nontrivial dimension-uniform family with index at most three.
entry.prior_rationale: The finite-index problem was formulated through the entanglement-breaking-index program in 2015 and remained open beyond unital, trace-preserving, faithful and other restricted PPT classes.
entry.advance_rationale: The theorem removes the remaining Perron-support restrictions and completes the qualitative finite-index problem for all PPT maps, while not resolving the stronger PPT-squared or uniform-index conjectures.
entry.scope_rationale: The theorem applies to PPT maps in every matrix dimension and all sufficiently large iterates of each map.
entry.resistance_rationale: Independent published results treated unital or trace-preserving PPT maps and later faithful PPT maps, providing two substantive partial approaches to the exact all-channel target.
entry.age_rationale: Elapsed duration is computed from the coded framing and solution dates; it is not a capability claim.

entry.description: Collision-Generated Compression for Homogeneous Keller Maps. The revised paper reports: We associate to a collision $p\ne q$ of a homogeneous Keller map $F=\operatorname{id}+h$ the polarization subalgebra generated by $p$ and $q$. This collision hull is the smallest invariant linear subspace containing the collision; the restricted map remains a noninjective Keller map, and its dimension controls that of the standard symmetric lift. The construction is compatible with scalar extension and equivariant under linear conjugacy, so it gives a canonical linear carrier for a marked failure of injectivity. We compute this carrier exactly in two recent cubic-homogeneous reductions of the three-variable Jacobian counterexample. For Thompson's 24-variable map, the growth $2,4,11,20,20$ recovers MacFarlane's 20-dimensional invariant subspace. For the 19-variable homogenization of Van Rijn's 12-variable degree-three map, the growth $2,4,11,19,19$ fills the whole space. Hence no invariant linear restriction retaining the displayed collision can improve the corresponding 38-variable symmetric lift. We give the resulting 340-monomial homogeneous quartic explicitly: it is Hessian-nilpotent, violates Zhao's Vanishing Conjecture, and its gradient Keller map has an exact collision over $\mathbb{Q}(i)$. The analogous 20-variable application gives the previously studied 40-variable, 350-monomial quartic. All finite calculations are checked by exact companion code. The primary source reports that ChatGPT and Codex extensively assisted literature work, maps, compression proofs, exact calculations, and drafting. entry.description: The Sharp Dimension Bound in the Johnson–Lindenstrauss Lemma. entry.description: Ollivier--Ricci Curvature on Groups of Polynomial Growth. For Cayley graphs of groups of polynomial growth, nonnegative Ollivier–Ricci curvature forces the group to be virtually abelian; consequently, a connected vertex-transitive graph of polynomial growth and nonnegative Ollivier–Ricci curvature is quasi-isometric to Z^k for some k. The authors attribute this AI role: ChatGPT 5.5 Thinking suggested a version of the potential used in §6.4, inspired the auxiliary-distance development in §6.3, checked the generator choice in Theorem 3.5, and suggested Remark 3.4; unused suggestions are explicitly separated by the authors.

entry.description: The cone theorem for effective fourfold pairs in characteristic $p>5$. Assuming the log resolution conjecture for all log pairs birational to $X$, we prove the cone theorem for projective log canonical, $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial fourfold pairs $(X,Δ)$ such that $K_X +Δ\equiv M \geq 0$ over bases of positive and mixed characteristic $p > 5$. The authors attribute this AI role: I worked out the outline of this proof with all essential ingredients, in Spring 2025. Unfortunately, there remained one gap that I could not repair. I gave the unfinished proof to ChatGPT 5.6 Sol in Summer 2026, asking it to fill the gap. It modified the approach to avoid the issue, which after further editing by hand and with Codex, resulted in the current version.

entry.description: A counterexample to a question on the maximality of purely-primes. For any integral domain k, the ring R=k[X₁,X₂,…]/(X_i(1−X_j):i<j) has a purely-prime ideal (the zero ideal) that is not purely-maximal, disproving Tarizadeh's Conjecture 5.8. The authors attribute this AI role: The paper says the counterexample in Theorem 2.5 was discovered with ChatGPT after Brian Conrad consulted the model; the author gives the full ring construction and proof.
